description: A STUDENT WHO HAS ALWAYS BEEN PASSIONATE ABOUT ASTRONOMY, PARTICULARLY OBSERVATIONAL ASTRONOMY
summary:
Still Answering is a single-page interactive story (HTML/CSS/JS, no dependencies) that re-frames the 796 pieces of human-made material left on the Moon and Mars — the "waste" in this challenge — as instruments still working.

What I developed: A scrolling, animated web experience built around four objects: Surveyor 3 (found still running by Apollo 12), the Apollo 11 Laser Retroreflector (measuring lunar distance for 57 years), Sojourner (first rover on Mars), and Voyager 1 (still transmitting from 24 billion km away). Each gets a short narrative and a "why it matters" fact card.

How it addresses the challenge: The problem statement asks about waste left behind. This project argues that what was "left" was never wasted — it's still generating science, still answering questions, still carrying our story outward. It shifts the framing from disposal to legacy.

Why it's important: Space exploration is accelerating. As we leave more hardware on other worlds, the public narrative around "abandoned" objects needs to change. This project makes that shift emotional and accessible — it ends by asking the reader what they would leave behind, turning a technical problem into a personal one.

Tech: Pure HTML/CSS/JS. Download and open in any browser. No build step, no server.
